assumptions: The account-wide people list is GET /users. The source only shows compact fields (gid, resource_type, name), so I request email with opt_fields; if Asana does not return it, email will be blank.

The source does not document status, role, created date, last-active, or guest/service type on GET /users, so those are not mapped. Suspended or deactivated users may not be distinguishable from active users.

Usage comes from workspace events. That call needs a workspace GID, and the provided source does not include a workspace-listing endpoint, so the workspace GID must be entered as a connection setting.
Workspace events return a sync token rather than a page number; I treat the sync token as the cursor and has_more as the stop flag.
No rate limits or error envelope are stated in the provided source, so those settings are left empty.
No paid-plan requirement was stated in the source for GET /users or workspace events; if Asana requires a specific plan, planRequirement will need to be set.

evidence.quote: We require that applications designed to access the Asana API on behalf of multiple users implement OAuth 2.0.
The list is always [paginated](/docs/pagination). When more results exist, the response includes a `next_page` with an `offset` that can be used to retrieve the next set of rows.
Returns the user records for all users in all workspaces and organizations accessible to the authenticated user.
Asana limits a single sync token to 1000 events. If more than 1000 events exist for a given domain, `has_more: true` will be returned in the response, indicating that there are more events to pull.
Returns the full record for all events that have occurred since the sync token was created.
